claims.value: 4 May 1504: revised contract with the Signoria, countersigned by Machiavelli
claims.statement: A deliberation of the Signoria dated 4 May 1504, signed by Niccolò Machiavelli as secretary, set terms for the cartoon (completion by the end of February 1505) and the painting. The exact text and witnesses were not read in this session.

claims.value: 6 June 1505: Leonardo's own note on beginning to paint, in a Madrid codex
claims.statement: A note in Leonardo's hand in one of the Madrid codices records that on Friday 6 June 1505 at the stroke of the thirteenth hour he began to paint in the Palazzo, with an accident of the weather. Codex and folio were not confirmed in this session (usually given as Madrid II).

claims.value: Agostino Vespucci's manuscript description of the battle for Leonardo
claims.statement: A manuscript text by Agostino Vespucci describing the battle of Anghiari, apparently prepared for Leonardo, is preserved in the Codex Atlanticus (folio to locate); a secondary source cites it as evidence of involvement from October 1503.

claims.value: Abandoned unfinished; known from copies and drawings
claims.statement: The mural was left unfinished when Leonardo left Florence in 1506 and later covered or destroyed in the remodelling of the hall; the composition of the central fight for the standard is known from copies and from preparatory drawings.

claims.value: Failure attributed to an experimental technique
claims.statement: That the painting failed because of an experimental oil based technique is an interpretation drawing on later narrative sources (Anonimo Gaddiano, Vasari), not a contemporary document.
